title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a table of the boundary stratifications of the Deligne–Mumford compactifications \bar M_{g,n} for small (g,n), drawn as stable dual graphs. Grothendieck's heading on the neighbouring pages is "Graphes MD", i.e. Mumford–Deligne graphs.

How the table is organised:
- Each row is labelled by (g,n).
- The right-hand column gives dim M_{g,n} = 3g-3+n: (0,3):0, (0,4):1, (0,5):2, (0,6):3, (1,1):1, (1,2):2, (1,3):3, (2,0):3, (2,1):4.
- Legs are unlabelled, so the strata are really those of \bar M_{g,n}/S_n.
- A vertex of positive genus carries its genus as a label; genus 0 is left unmarked, as page 127 prescribes.
- Each graph sits one column further right per edge, so the column is the codimension.
- An arrow G -> G' means G' is obtained by contracting one edge of G, i.e. the stratum of G lies in the closure of the stratum of G'.
- The integer on an arrow counts the edges of G whose contraction gives G' (the number of local branches).

Checks, row by row:
- (0,4): one vertex <- the 2+2 tree.
- (0,5): one vertex <- the 3+2 tree <-(2)- the chain 2,1,2.
- (0,6): codimension 1 has the 3+3 and 4+2 trees. Codimension 2 has the chains (3,1,2) and (2,2,2). Codimension 3 has the chain (2,1,1,2) and the tripod with leaves (2,2,2).
  - The chain (2,1,1,2) maps to (3,1,2) with multiplicity 2, and to (2,2,2) by contracting its middle edge.
  - The tripod maps to (2,2,2) with multiplicity 3.
  - (2,2,2) maps to the 4+2 tree with multiplicity 2.
  - (3,1,2) maps to both 3+3 and 4+2.
  All of this is correct and complete.
- (1,1): the vertex of genus 1 <- the nodal rational curve (a loop).
- (1,2): codimension 1 has the loop vertex with 2 legs and the genus-1 vertex joined to a vertex with 2 legs. Codimension 2 has the 2-cycle (double edge, 1+1 legs), which maps to the loop vertex with multiplicity 2, and loop–vertex(2 legs). This is complete.
- (1,3): all codimension 1, 2 and 3 strata appear, including the three maximal ones:
  - the triangle, mapping to the double-edge graph with multiplicity 3;
  - the double edge followed by a vertex with 2 legs;
  - the chain loop–vertex(1 leg)–vertex(2 legs).
  The crossed arrows record the double incidences.
- (2,0): the seven strata of \bar M_2.
  - Codimension 1: the vertex of genus 1 with a loop, and two genus-1 vertices joined by an edge.
  - Codimension 2: the figure-eight (genus-0 vertex with two loops), mapping to the genus-1 loop vertex with multiplicity 2; and the genus-1 vertex joined to a loop vertex.
  - Codimension 3: the theta graph, mapping to the figure-eight with multiplicity 3; and the dumbbell, mapping to the figure-eight with multiplicity 1 and to (genus-1)–(loop vertex) with multiplicity 2.
- (2,1): only begun, with a few codimension-1 graphs and then "......". Dimension 4.

Purpose: this serves the Teichmüller-groupoid / "Teichmüller tower" programme of file 146. The aim is to understand how boundary strata of the \bar M_{g,n} (the "points at infinity", tangential base points) glue together, and to see that the low-dimensional pieces, (0,4) and (1,1) in dimension 1, together with dimension 2, control everything. Page 127 then formalises the stable weighted graphs as (S, half-edges, origin map o, involution σ, genus g), with legs taken as the fixed points of σ, the stability condition 2g_s + ν_s ≥ 3, and the formulas for codimension and virtual genus.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. Every incidence and multiplicity I checked is correct.
The (2,1) row is left unfinished, marked '......'.
The multiplicity on the dumbbell -> figure-eight arrow is written as an unclear symbol (transcribed 'ε'). The correct value is 1.

ideas.what: Stratification of \bar M_{g,n} by stable dual graphs, with the incidence (specialisation) poset given by edge contractions
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of the Deligne–Mumford compactification by stable graphs; the category or poset of stable graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen; graph formalism by Kontsevich–Manin 1994 and Getzler–Kapranov 1998 (modular operads)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and the stratification at infinity, but not these explicit tables

ideas.what: Arrows labelled with the number of edges whose contraction gives the target graph (number of local branches of the boundary stratum)
ideas.modern_name: Incidence multiplicities in the boundary complex; the coefficients of the graph-complex / Feynman-transform differential before orientation

ideas.what: Explicit enumeration of the strata of \bar M_{g,n}/S_n for 2g-2+n small, with dimension 3g-3+n, including all 7 strata of \bar M_2
ideas.modern_name: Census of boundary strata (stable graphs) of low-dimensional moduli spaces

missed.claim: Taken with page 127, this is an early (around 1978–81) systematic use of stable graphs as combinatorial bookkeeping for the boundary of \bar M_{g,n}. Page 127 uses the half-edge/involution formalism with legs as fixed points of σ, a formalism usually credited to Kontsevich–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov in the 1990s. This page itself contains only standard, correct enumerations.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it documents Grothendieck anticipating the modular-operad graph formalism by about 15 years. Mathematically there is nothing new.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct but standard table of boundary strata and contraction incidences for small \bar M_{g,n}. Its interest is mainly historical: the early date and its link to the stable-graph formalism on the next page. It holds no new result.
transcription_corrections: (0,3) is one vertex with 3 legs; the right-hand column numbers are the dimensions 3g-3+n.

(0,6): the codimension-1 graphs are the 3+3 tree (upper) and the 4+2 tree (lower, 'X' shape). The codimension-2 chains are (3,1,2) (upper) and (2,2,2) (lower; its arrow to 4+2 has multiplicity 2). The 4-vertex chain (2,1,1,2) maps to (3,1,2) with label 2 and to (2,2,2) without a label. The tripod with three 2-leg leaves maps to (2,2,2) with label 3.
(1,2): the double-edge graph maps to the loop vertex with 2 legs with label 2; loop–vertex(2 legs) maps both to the loop vertex and to [genus 1]–vertex(2 legs).

(2,0): the theta graph maps to the figure-eight with label 3. The dumbbell (loop–loop) maps to the figure-eight (unclear symbol, value 1) and to [genus 1]–loop vertex with label 2. The figure-eight maps to the genus-1 vertex with a loop with label 2. [genus 1]–loop vertex maps to both the genus-1 vertex with a loop and [genus 1]–[genus 1].
(2,1): the drawn graphs are the genus-2 vertex with a leg, the genus-1 vertex with a loop and a leg, and two genus-1 vertices joined by an edge with a leg, followed by '......'.
